tagline: Up a valley drawn with a ruler.
intro: From Jasper, near the southern end, TN 28 heads north up the Sequatchie Valley between Walden Ridge and the Cumberland Plateau, the walls rising about a thousand feet above a floor only three to five miles wide. The valley is remarked on for its straightness, nearly perfect from end to end. At Dunlap the road becomes US 127 and carries on through Pikeville, then climbs onto the plateau to Crossville.
The Cherokee ceded the valley in 1805. Coal came later, dug from the mountains and baked into coke at their feet.

moments.title: Whitwell
moments.text: In this mining town a German railcar holds 11 million paper clips, gathered by middle school students in a project begun in 1998 to teach tolerance.

moments.title: Dunlap Coke Ovens
moments.text: Just west of Dunlap, five batteries of 268 beehive ovens at the foot of Fredonia Mountain once turned the mountain's coal into coke for blast furnaces in Chattanooga.

moments.title: Pikeville
moments.text: The county seat since 1818 sends US 127 north up the mountain on a stretch that a Vanderbilt engineering student helped build during a summer job.
